To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biochemical pattern of ascitic fluid in neoplastic disease is different from that in liver cirrhotic ascites.

the combination of biochemical parameters of the ascitic liquid can be used as a reliable diagnostic tool in the differentiation between neoplastic and non-neoplastic ascites, and that it is a simple, fast, and inexpensive method.

1) the cluster analysis of biochemical pattern of the ascetic fluid, in liver cirrhoses and in neoplasms, is able to recognize correctly most of the cases; 2) the sensitivity and the specificity of this procedure, for the diagnosis of malignancy in ascites, are respectively 89% and 82%; 3) the procedure can be used in clinical practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the biochemical pattern of ascitic fluid.
the evaluation of biochemical pattern in ascitic fluid in order to discriminate liver cirrhosis from malignant diseases.
the study of ascitic fluid in patients with liver cirrhoses and in patients with neoplastic diseases, both with ascitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ascitic fluid is a very useful source of biochemical information for diagnosis of malignancy and of liver cirrhosis.

the ascitic fluid biochemical pattern in liver cirrhoses is different from the one of the ascitic fluids of neoplastic diseases, but the difference is not so marked to permit a correct diagnosis in each single case.
the biochemical pattern of ascitic fluid is not able to differentiate between cirrhosis and cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in ascites, the biochemical pattern of the ascites fluid is able to discriminate correctly between liver cirrhosis with ascites and malignancy with ascites.
ascitic fluid analysis is useful for the differential diagnosis of cirrhosis and malignancy.

, in a patient with liver cirrhoses and ascites, if the ascites is found to be of low protein content, it is unlikely that malignancy is present; if it is found to have a high protein content, the possibility of a malignant disease must be considered.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biochemical analysis of ascites can be a useful diagnostic tool for the differential diagnosis of ascites in liver cirrhoses and in neoplasms.
the biochemical analysis of ascites is a useful diagnostic tool for differentiating liver cirrhosis from malignancy.
the ascitic fluid is an excellent source for biomarkers of cancer and cirrhosis.
